translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue chopped Jun’s left hand—Jun wheeled and took his sword arm.

sentences.zh: 武衛之士皆趨上殿，峻云：「所取者恪也，今已死。

translations.literal: Palace guards rushed the hall—Jun shouted, “We seek only Ke—he is already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Guards stormed in—“Only Ke—he is dead.

sentences.zh: 」悉令復刃，乃除地更飲。

translations.literal: He ordered all to sheath weapons; the floor was cleared and drinking resumed.
translations.idiomatic: Blades went home; blood was mopped and cups refilled.

sentences.zh: 〈《搜神記》曰：恪入，已被殺，其妻在室，語使婢曰：「汝何故血臭？

translations.literal: The Sou shen ji says: After Ke entered he was slain; his wife indoors asked her maid, “Why this stench of blood?”
translations.idiomatic: Sou shen ji: Ke’s widow smelled gore on her maid.

sentences.zh: 」婢曰：「不也。

translations.literal: The maid said, “It is not so.”
translations.idiomatic: “There is none,” said the girl.

sentences.zh: 」有頃愈劇，又問婢曰：「汝眼目視瞻，何以不常？

translations.literal: Presently it grew worse; she asked again, “Why do your eyes dart so strangely?”
translations.idiomatic: The smell thickened—“Why do your eyes roll?” she pressed.

sentences.zh: 」婢蹶然起躍，頭至於棟，攘臂切齒而言曰：「諸葛公乃為孫峻所殺！

translations.literal: The maid sprang upright, head brushing the rafters, flailing arms and gnashing teeth: “Lord Zhuge has been murdered by Sun Jun!”
translations.idiomatic: The maid convulsed to the beams—“Sun Jun killed Zhuge Ke!”

sentences.zh: 」於是大小知恪死矣，而吏兵尋至。

translations.literal: Then great and small knew Ke was dead—and soldiers arrived moments later.
translations.idiomatic: The household understood—troops hammered the gate next.

sentences.zh: 《志林》曰：初權病篤，召恪輔政。

translations.literal: The Zhi lin says: When Sun Quan first fell gravely ill he summoned Ke to aid governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi lin records Quan’s deathbed summons of Ke.

sentences.zh: 臨去，大司馬呂岱戒之曰：「世方多難，子每事必十思。

translations.literal: As Ke departed, Grand Marshal Lü Dai warned him: “The age bristles with trouble—in every matter reflect ten times.”
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Lü Dai saw him off: “Think ten times on each step.”

sentences.zh: 」恪答曰：「昔季文子三思而後行，夫子曰『再思可矣』，今君令恪十思，明恪之劣也。

translations.literal: Ke replied, “Of old Jiwenzi reflected thrice before acting—the Master said ‘Twice suffices’—now you bid me reflect ten times—you proclaim my incompetence.”
translations.idiomatic: Ke quoted Confucius—“Twice is enough”—“Ten times insults my wit.”

sentences.zh: 」岱無以答，當時咸謂之失言。

translations.literal: Dai had no reply—contemporaries all called him wrong-footed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai stood mute—onlookers jeered his silence.

sentences.zh: 虞喜曰：夫託以天下至重也，以人臣行主威至難也，兼二至而管萬機，能勝之者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Yu Xi remarks: Entrusting All-under-Heaven is weight supreme; wielding royal awe as minister is hardship supreme—bearing both while steering myriad threads—few master it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi: regency is the heaviest trust—few bear throne and sword together.

sentences.zh: 自非採納群謀，詢於芻蕘，虛己受人，恆若不足，則功名不成，勳績莫著。

translations.literal: Unless one gathers counsel from all, inquires even of grass cutters, empties self to accept others, forever feeling insufficient—merit will not stand and deeds will not shine.
translations.idiomatic: Without humble ears open to every voice, fame founders.

sentences.zh: 況呂侯國之先耆，智度經遠，而甫以十思戒之，而便以示劣見拒，此元遜之疏，乃機神不俱者也。

translations.literal: Moreover Grand Marshal Lü was the realm’s elder statesman, his judgment far-seeing—yet at first counsel he warned with “reflect ten times,” only to meet rejection as proof of weakness—this was Yuansun’s obtuseness; wit and nerve did not march together.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai was veteran sage—his “think ten times” was rope thrown to a drowning man; Ke sneered—clever tongue, hollow nerve.

sentences.zh: 若因十思之義，廣諮當世之務，聞善速於雷動，從諫急於風移，豈得隕首殿堂，死兇豎之刃？

translations.literal: Had Ke taken that tenfold reflection as cue to canvass the age’s tasks, hearing good like thunder’s roll, heeding remonstrance swift as wind’s shift—would he have fallen headless in the hall, dying on a boy villain’s blade?
translations.idiomatic: Had he listened like lightning—would he lie headless to Jun’s knife?

sentences.zh: 世人奇其英辯，造次可觀，而哂呂侯無對為陋，不思安危終始之慮，是樂春藻之繁華，而忘秋實之甘口也。

translations.literal: The age marvels at his eloquent repartee, dazzling in haste, and mocks Lü Hou’s silence as crude—never pondering safety from first to last—they savor spring blossoms’ flourish and forget autumn fruit’s sweetness.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds praise Ke’s wit and laugh at Lü—but eloquence without judgment is savoring blossom while ignoring harvest.

sentences.zh: 昔魏人伐蜀，蜀人御之，精嚴垂發，六軍雲擾，士馬擐甲，羽檄交馳，費禕時為元帥，荷國任重，而與來敏圍棋，意無厭倦。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Shu resisted—discipline taut as bowstrings about to loose, six hosts cloud-turbulent, men and horses mailed, feather dispatches crisscrossing—Fei Yi then held marshal’s baton, shouldering the state’s weight, yet played weiqi with Lai Min, weariness nowhere seen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck Shu—Fei Yi, burdened with command, played go with Lai Min amid flying orders.

sentences.zh: 敏臨別謂禕：「君必能辦賊者也。

translations.literal: As Min parted he told Yi, “You will surely master these bandits.”
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min left saying, “You will break them.”

sentences.zh: 」言其明略內定，貌無憂色，況長寧以為君子臨事而懼，好謀而成者。

translations.literal: He meant Yi’s strategy was fixed within though his face showed no fear—moreover Changning deemed the gentleman fearful at affairs yet completes plans through counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He read calm as settled strategy—the gentleman fears, then wins by plotting.

sentences.zh: 且蜀為蕞爾之國，而方向大敵，所規所圖，唯守與戰，何可矜己有餘，晏然無戚？

translations.literal: Moreover Shu was a tiny state facing a great foe—its schemes aimed solely at defense and battle—how could one pride oneself on surplus ease and sit tranquil without anxiety?
translations.idiomatic: Tiny Shu faced giant Wei—how boast ease with survival at stake?

sentences.zh: 斯乃性之寬簡，不防細微，卒為降人郭脩所害，豈非兆見於彼而禍成於此哉？

translations.literal: Such was nature broad and careless of detail—thereupon he fell to the surrendered man Guo Xiu—is this not an omen manifest there while calamity matured here?
translations.idiomatic: His loose temper missed fine hazard—so Guo Xiu the turncoat cut him down—warning ignored, blade earned.

sentences.zh: 往聞長寧之甄文偉，今睹元遜之逆呂侯，二事體同，故並而載之，可以鏡誡於後，永為世鑑。〉

translations.literal: Formerly I heard Zhangning’s critique of Wen Wei; now I witness Yuansun’s riposte to Marquis Lü—the two cases mirror each other—therefore I join them in one note so posterity may take warning and the world hold them forever as mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi pairs Zhuge Ke’s barb at Lü Dai with an older spat—both cautionary tales worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 先是，童謠曰：「諸葛恪，蘆葦單衣蔑鉤落，於何相求成子閣。

translations.literal: Earlier a children’s rhyme ran: “Zhuge Ke—rush cloak, hemp belt, hook-falls dangling—where shall we seek you but Chengzi Pavilion?”
translations.idiomatic: A street rhyme foretold Ke: reed mat, hemp coat, belt-hooks dangling—seek him at “Chengzi Pavilion.”

sentences.zh: 」成子閣者，反語石子岡也。

translations.literal: “Chengzi Pavilion” reversed yields Shizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Flip the syllables—“Chengzi” hides Shizi Gang.

sentences.zh: 建業面有長陵，名曰石子岡，葬者依焉。

translations.literal: East of Jianye lies a long mound called Shizi Ridge—burials crowd there.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Jianye stands the burial mound Shizi Gang—Wu’s potter’s field.

sentences.zh: 鉤落者，校飾革帶，世謂之鉤絡帶。

translations.literal: “Hook-falls” means ornamented leather belt gear—the folk call it hooked-net belts.
translations.idiomatic: The hooks mean fancy belt fittings commoners called “hook-lattice” straps.

sentences.zh: 恪果以葦席裹其身而篾束其腰，投之於此岡。

translations.literal: Ke indeed was rolled in a rush mat, his waist lashed with bamboo strips, and cast on that ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They wound him in reed mat and bamboo cord and dumped him on Shizi Gang.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：恪時年五十一。〉

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Ke was fifty-one sui at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lu notes Ke died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 恪長子綽，騎都尉，以交關魯王事，權遣付恪，令更教誨，恪鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Ke’s eldest son Chuo was Cavalry Commandant; for dealings with the Prince of Lu, Quan handed him to Ke ordering renewed instruction—Ke poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Zhuge Chuo, tied to the Lu prince scandal, was handed back to Ke for discipline—Ke murdered him with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 中子辣，長水校尉。

translations.literal: Middle son Song (received text gives an aberrant graph for the personal name), Colonel of Long Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: His middle son Zhuge Song held the colonelcy on the Long River.

sentences.zh: 少子建，步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Youngest son Jian was Colonel of Foot.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest Zhuge Jian commanded camp foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 聞恪誅，車載其母而走。

translations.literal: When news came that Ke had been executed they loaded his mother on a cart and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His household carted the mother away at news of the coup.

sentences.zh: 峻遣騎督承追斬竦於白都。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched Cavalry Supervisor Cheng to pursue and strike him dead at Baidu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun’s riders ran Ke’s fleeing son down at Baidu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 建得渡江，欲北走魏，行數千里，為追兵所逮。

translations.literal: Jian crossed the Yangzi intending to flee north to Wei; after traveling thousands of li he was overtaken by pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jian made the river but Wei caught him a thousand li north.

sentences.zh: 恪外甥都鄉侯張震及常侍朱恩等，皆夷三族。

translations.literal: Ke’s nephew Zhang Zhen, marquis of Duxiang, and Palace Attendant Zhu En and others—all three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Zhang Zhen of Duxiang and Zhu En died with their kin to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 初，竦數諫恪，恪不從，常憂懼禍。

translations.literal: Earlier Song had remonstrated Ke repeatedly; Ke ignored him and Song lived in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Song had warned his brother again and again—terror followed silence.

sentences.zh: 及亡，臨淮臧均表乞收葬恪曰：

translations.literal: After his death Zang Jun of Linhuai memorialized begging leave to gather Ke’s corpse for burial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zang Jun of Linhuai then petitioned for decent burial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞震雷電激，不崇一朝，大風沖發，殺有極日。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that thunderbolts do not thunder endlessly nor gales blow without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thunderclaps end; hurricanes taper—even heaven moderates rage.

sentences.zh: 然猶繼以雲雨，因以潤物，是則天地之威，不可經日浹辰，帝王之怒，不宜訖情盡意，臣以狂愚，不知忌諱，敢冒破滅之罪，以邀風雨之會。

translations.literal: Yet rain follows cloud and thereby moistens creatures—thus Heaven-Earth’s awe cannot span days without pause; an emperor’s wrath ought not exhaust feeling to the last drop. I, mad and foolish, ignorant of taboo, dare risk ruin to invite the season of calming rain.
translations.idiomatic: Storms give way to soaking rain—so should a throne ease after wrath. I risk my neck to beg that mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏念故太傅諸葛恪得承祖考風流之烈，伯叔諸父遭漢祚盡，九州鼎立，分托三方，並履忠勤，熙隆世業。

translations.literal: I reflect that the late Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke inherited the fierce virtue of ancestors and forebears; uncles and fathers met Han’s exhausted mandate—nine provinces stood tripod-wise—each branch lodged with one realm, alike treading loyalty and toil, magnifying the family enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuges served three kingdoms with loyal sweat—Ke inherited that fire.

sentences.zh: 爰及於恪，生長王國，陶育聖化，致名英偉，服事累紀，禍心未萌，先帝委以伊、週之任，屬以萬機之事。

translations.literal: Down to Ke he grew within the royal domain, molded by sagely transformation, achieving famed brilliance; he served many reigns without treason stirring—then the late emperor entrusted him with Yi-Yin and Duke of Zhou’s burden and hung myriad threads upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke grew up at court, served honorably, then took regency meant for Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 恪索性剛履，矜己陵人，不能敬守神器，穆靜幫內，興功暴師，未期三出，虛耗士民，空竭府藏，專擅國憲，廢易由意，假刑劫眾，大小屏息。

translations.literal: Ke’s nature was sheer rigidity—he prized self and trampled others; he failed to honor the regalia in reverent quiet within the state; he raised hosts and exposed armies—three expeditions within a year—draining soldiers and folk, emptying treasuries; he monopolized statutes, cashiered and appointed at whim, borrowed punishments to cow the masses—great and small held breath.
translations.idiomatic: He seized law, burned treasure and men on vain wars, ruled by terror.

sentences.zh: 侍中武衛將軍都鄉候俱受先帝囑寄之詔，見其奸虐，日月滋甚，將恐蕩搖宇宙，傾危社稷，奮其威怒，精貫昊天，計慮先於神明，智勇百於荊、聶，躬持白刃，梟恪殿堂，勳超朱，功越東牟。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant, General Who Guards the Martial, Marquis of Duxiang—both bore the late emperor’s testamentary edict; seeing Ke’s wicked cruelty swell day by day, fearing he would shake the cosmos and overturn altars of soil and grain, they roused awesome wrath, essence piercing the azure sky, counsel anticipating gods, wit and daring surpassing Jing Ke and Nie Zheng; gripping naked blades they struck Ke’s head in the hall—merit exceeding Zhu Hai, deeds outdoing Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun, testament guardian and guard general, struck Ke down in the throne hall and hailed it as salvation for temple and throne.

sentences.zh: 國之元害，一朝大除，馳首徇示，六軍喜踴，日月增光，風塵不動，斯實宗廟之神靈，天人之同驗也。

translations.literal: The realm’s arch villain perished in one dawn; his head was paraded as warning—the Six Armies leapt for joy, sun and moon seemed brighter, dust did not stir—truly spirits of the ancestral temple and sign shared by Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Ke’s fall drew cheers—soldiers called it heaven’s verdict.

sentences.zh: 今恪父子三首，懸市積日，觀者數萬，詈聲成風。

translations.literal: Now father and sons’ three heads hang in market days uncounted—tens of thousands watch; curses rise like wind.
translations.idiomatic: Three heads rotted on public display while crowds jeered.

sentences.zh: 國之大刑，無所不震，長老孩幼，無不畢見。

translations.literal: When great punishments fall none escape trembling—elders and babes alike witness all.
translations.idiomatic: State terror teaches every age.

sentences.zh: 人情之於品物，樂極則哀生，見恪貴盛，世莫與貳，身處台輔，中間歷年，今之誅夷，無異禽獸，觀訖情反，能不憯然！

translations.literal: Human feeling toward things turns sorrow after joy’s peak—seeing Ke’s glory none could rival while he stood pillar of state years on end, today’s extermination no different from beasts—when viewing ends feeling reverses—who fails to ache?
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday’s idol is today’s carrion—pity follows spite.

sentences.zh: 且已死之人，與土壤同域，鑿掘斫刺，無所復加。

translations.literal: Moreover the dead share earth with soil—digging, hacking, stabbing adds nothing further.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses need no further desecration.

sentences.zh: 願聖朝稽則乾坤，怒不極旬，使其鄉邑若故吏民收以士伍之服，惠以三寸之棺。

translations.literal: May the sage court mirror Heaven-Earth—let wrath not span full ten days—allow hometown veterans and old clerks to dress him in soldier’s garb and favor a three-inch coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Grant plain wood armor and a thin coffin—rage enough.

sentences.zh: 昔項籍受殯葬之施，韓信獲收斂之恩，斯則漢高發神明之譽也。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu received burial kindness; Han Xin won winding-sheet grace—there Han Gaozu earned reputation as spirit-clear.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu buried enemies with honor—so should Wu.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下敦三皇之仁，垂哀矜之心，使國澤加於辜戮之骸，復受不已之恩，於以揚聲遐方，沮勸天下，豈不弘哉！

translations.literal: May Your Majesty thicken Three August Ones’ benevolence, extend pity’s heart, let state kindness touch slaughtered bones, grant ceaseless grace—thereby spreading fame afar, checking and encouraging All-under-Heaven—how vast!
translations.idiomatic: Mercy to the executed advertises virtue empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 昔欒布矯命彭越，臣竊恨之，不先請主上，而專名以肆情，其得不誅，實為幸耳。

translations.literal: Of old Luan Bu forged orders for Peng Yue—I secretly resented he did not first petition his lord but seized sole fame to vent private feeling; that he escaped execution was mere luck.
translations.idiomatic: Luan Bu acted without imperial OK—I condemn his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 今臣不敢章宣愚情以露天恩，謹伏手書，冒昧陳聞，乞聖朝哀察。

translations.literal: Now your servant dares not proclaim foolish feeling aloud to expose heavenly grace—I humbly submit this private script, bluntly stating my plea; begging the sage court pity and examine.
translations.idiomatic: I seal this plea—not for spectacle but for mercy.

sentences.zh: 於是亮、峻聽恪故吏斂葬，遂求之於石子岡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang and Jun allowed Ke’s former clerks to wrap him for burial and sought the corpse at Shizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The regents let old aides recover Ke from Shizi Gang.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：朝臣有乞為恪立碑以銘其勳績者，博士盛衝以為不應。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan says: Courtiers petitioned to raise a stele engraving Ke’s deeds—Doctor Sheng Chong argued against.
translations.idiomatic: Some wanted a monument—Doctor Sheng Chong refused.

sentences.zh: 孫休曰：「盛夏出軍，士卒傷損，無尺寸之功，不可謂能；

translations.literal: Sun Xiu said: “To march midsummer wounding troops without inch-wide merit—cannot be called able;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu judged: “Summer war without gain is not skill;

sentences.zh: 受託孤之任，死於豎子之手，不可謂智。

translations.literal: to bear orphan-entrustment yet die at a boy’s hand—cannot be called wise.”
translations.idiomatic: to die regent at a stripling’s blade is not wisdom.”

sentences.zh: 衝議為是。

translations.literal: Chong’s opinion was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Chong had the right of it.

sentences.zh: 」遂寢。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter slept.
translations.idiomatic: The stele died unraised.

sentences.zh: 始恪退軍還，聶友知其將敗。

translations.literal: When Ke first withdrew his army Nie You knew he would fall.
translations.idiomatic: Nie You saw doom in Ke’s retreat.

sentences.zh: 書與滕胤曰：「當人強盛，河山可拔，一朝羸縮，人情萬端，言之悲歎。

translations.literal: He wrote Teng Yin: “While a man towers mountains and rivers may yield—once strength shrinks human moods multiply ten thousand ways—speech turns to lament.”
translations.idiomatic: He warned Yin: power ebbs—crowds turn cruel overnight.

sentences.zh: 」恪誅後，孫峻忌友，欲以為鬱林太守。

translations.literal: After Ke’s execution Sun Jun envied You and wished to appoint him governor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Jun hated Nie You and tried to exile him to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 友發病憂死。

translations.literal: You sickened with worry and died.
translations.idiomatic: Nie You worried himself to death.

sentences.zh: 友字文悌，豫章人也。

translations.literal: You, courtesy name Wendi, was a man of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Nie You (Wendi), from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：友有脣吻，少為縣吏。

translations.literal: The Wu lu says: You had a ready tongue and young served as county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lu calls him glib—started as county clerk.

sentences.zh: 虞翻徙交州，縣令使友送之，翻與語而奇焉，為書與豫章太守謝斐，令以為功曹。

translations.literal: When Yu Fan was banished to Jiaozhou the county magistrate sent You to escort him; Fan spoke with him and marveled, writing Yuzhang Governor Xie Fei to appoint him Clerk of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan spotted his wit en route to exile and recommended him to Xie Fei.

sentences.zh: 郡時見有功曹，斐見之，問曰：「縣吏聶友，可堪何職？

translations.literal: The commandery then lacked a Clerk of Merit—when Fei met him he asked, “County clerk Nie You—which office fits?”
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fei asked what post suited the clerk.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此人縣間小吏耳，猶可堪曹佐。

translations.literal: He answered, “This man is only a petty county clerk—still fit for aide posts.”
translations.idiomatic: “Barely fit for a bureau aide,” came reply.

sentences.zh: 」斐曰：「論者以為宜作功曹，君其避之。

translations.literal: Fei said, “Critics deem him proper Clerk of Merit—you should yield the seat.”
translations.idiomatic: “Men say merit clerk—step aside,” Fei ordered.

sentences.zh: 」乃用為功曹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he employed him as Clerk of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Nie You became merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 使至都，諸葛恪友之。

translations.literal: When dispatched to the capital Zhuge Ke befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Ke made him a confidant.

sentences.zh: 時論謂顧子嘿、子直，其間無所复容，恪欲以友居其間，由是知名。

translations.literal: Current opinion held no room between Gu Zimo and Gu Zizhi—Ke wished to seat You between them—thereby You rose to fame.
translations.idiomatic: Fashion ranked Gu Tan cousins supreme—Ke slid Nie between them for reputation.

sentences.zh: 後為將，討儋耳，還拜丹楊太守，年三十三卒。〉

translations.literal: Later he became general, campaigned against Dan’er, returned as Danyang governor, died at thirty-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: He led the Dan’er expedition, ruled Danyang, died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 恪將悉眾伐魏。

translations.literal: Ke was about to lead the entire host against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke prepared another full-scale strike on Wei.

sentences.zh: 胤諫恪曰：「君以喪代之際，受伊、霍之託，入安本朝，出摧強敵，名聲振於海內，天下莫不震動，萬姓之心，冀得蒙君而息。

translations.literal: Yin remonstrated Ke: “You amid succession crisis accepted Yi-Huo trust—within you steadied court, without broke mighty foes—fame thundered within the seas so none failed to tremble—myriad households hoped to lean on you and catch breath.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin urged restraint: the empire needed breathing space after Ke’s early victories, not another whirlwind march.

sentences.zh: 今猥以勞役之後，興師出征，民疲力屈，遠主有備。

translations.literal: Now on the heels of weary labor you raise armies—the people are spent, distant foe stands warned.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from exhaustion you march—foe waits fresh.

sentences.zh: 若攻城不克，野略無獲，是喪前勞而招後責也。

translations.literal: If siege fails and field foray yields naught you waste prior toil and invite later blame.
translations.idiomatic: Fail twice and you buy shame not glory.

sentences.zh: 不如案甲息師，觀隙而動。

translations.literal: Better sheath blades, rest troops, watch opportunities.
translations.idiomatic: Cool your spears—wait for a seam.

sentences.zh: 且兵者大事，事以眾濟，眾苟不悅，君獨安之？

translations.literal: Moreover war is great affair—success needs mass support—if masses chafe can you stand alone secure?”
translations.idiomatic: War needs popular heart—can you ride hatred?”

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「諸雲不可者，皆不見計算，懷居苟安者也，而子復以為然，吾何望焉？

translations.literal: Ke said, “All who cry impossible lack reckoning and hug hearth ease—you echo them—what hope remains?
translations.idiomatic: Ke sneered: cowards and calculators—you too?

sentences.zh: 夫以曹勞暗劣，而政在私門，彼之臣民，固有離心。

translations.literal: With Cao Fang dim-witted and government in private hands their ministers and people already nurse divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s boy emperor drools while regents feud—ripe rot within.

sentences.zh: 今吾因國家之資，借戰勝之威，則何往而不克哉！

translations.literal: Now if I ride our state’s resources and borrow victory’s prestige—where shall I march and not break?”
translations.idiomatic: Give me our surplus and last win—where is steel we cannot pierce?”

sentences.zh: 」以胤為都下督，掌統留事。

translations.literal: He appointed Yin Capital Commandant directing rear-area affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yin to govern the capital rear.

sentences.zh: 胤白日接賓客，夜省文書，或通曉不寐。

translations.literal: Yin received guests by daylight, reviewed documents by night—sometimes dawn found him sleepless.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin lived at desk and gate—nights without sleep.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：胤寵任彌高，接士愈勤，表奏書疏，皆自經意，不以委下。〉

translations.literal: The Wu shu says: Yin’s favor mounted—he grew busier courting scholars; memorials and correspondence he penned himself, delegating nothing below.
translations.idiomatic: Wu shu praises his hands-on paperwork.

sentences.zh: 二年，魏毋丘儉、文欽以眾叛，與魏人戰於樂嘉，峻帥驃騎將軍呂據、左將軍留贊襲壽春，會欽敗降，軍還。

translations.literal: Second year—Wei’s Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled with hosts and fought Wei at Lejia—Jun led General of Agile Cavalry Lü Ju and General of the Left Liu Zan to raid Shouchun—when Qin lost and surrendered troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: Year two: Jian and Qin rose at Lejia; Sun Jun struck toward Shouchun with Lü Ju and Liu Zan—Qin collapsed and Wu marched home.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：留贊字正明，會稽長山人。

translations.literal: The Wu shu says: Liu Zan, courtesy name Zhengming, was a man of Changshan in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wu shu: Liu Zan (Zhengming) of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，與黃巾賊帥吳桓戰，手斬得桓。

translations.literal: Youth as county clerk—fought Yellow Turban chief Wu Huan and personally slew Huan.
translations.idiomatic: As clerk he beheaded Turban chief Wu Huan hand-to-hand.

sentences.zh: 贊一足被創，遂屈不伸。

translations.literal: Zan took a wound to one foot—it thereafter stayed bent and would not straighten.
translations.idiomatic: A spear lame left his foot frozen bent.

sentences.zh: 然性烈，好讀兵書及三史，每覽古良將戰攻之勢，輒對書獨嘆，因呼諸近親謂曰：「今天下擾亂，英豪並起，歷觀前世，富貴非有常人，而我屈躄在閭巷之間，存亡無以異。

translations.literal: Yet nature fierce—he loved reading military works and the Three Histories—whenever scanning ancient champions’ battles he sighed alone over the text then called kin near: “All-under-Heaven is chaos—heroes rise together—scanning former ages wealth and honor favor no fixed men—yet I hobble alley-bound—life or death no different.”
translations.idiomatic: He studied war yet limped—burned to matter.

sentences.zh: 今欲割引吾足，幸不死而足申，幾復見用，死則已矣。

translations.literal: “Now I wish to slice and stretch my foot—if I live with foot straightened I may see employment again—death ends it.”
translations.idiomatic: “Cut the sinew—straight foot or death.”

sentences.zh: 」親戚皆難之。

translations.literal: Kinsmen all opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Family forbade the knife.

sentences.zh: 有間，贊乃以刀自割其筋，血流滂沱，氣絕良久。

translations.literal: After a pause Zan took knife and cut his own sinews—blood gushed—breath stopped long while.
translations.idiomatic: He sawed his tendons—blood flood—fainted.

sentences.zh: 家人驚怖，亦以既爾，遂引申其足。

translations.literal: Household panicked—since done already they forced the foot straight.
translations.idiomatic: Kin splinted the leg straight.

sentences.zh: 足申創愈，以得蹉步。

translations.literal: Foot straightened—wound healed—he could hobble.
translations.idiomatic: Healed, he limped to battle.

sentences.zh: 凌統聞之，請與相見，甚奇之，乃表薦贊，遂被試用。

translations.literal: Ling Tong heard, asked interview, marveled, memorialized recommendation—Zan won trial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong sponsored him into service.

sentences.zh: 累有戰功，稍遷屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Repeated battle merit—gradually promoted Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns raised him to Garrison Cavalry colonel.

sentences.zh: 時事得失，每常規諫，好直言不阿旨，權以此憚之。

translations.literal: On policy gains and losses he routinely remonstrated—loving blunt speech without flattering edicts—Quan therefore feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke truth Sun Quan disliked.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪征東興，讚為前部，合戰先陷陳，大敗魏師，遷左將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Ke campaigned Dongxing Zan led van—joined battle first breaking lines—greatly defeated Wei hosts—promoted General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Van at Dongxing—first through Wei lines—left general.

sentences.zh: 孫峻徵淮南，授贊節，拜左護軍。

translations.literal: When Sun Jun campaigned Huainan Zan received insignia as Guard-General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s Huainan march made him credentialed left guard.

sentences.zh: 未至壽春，道路病發，峻令贊將車重先還。

translations.literal: Before reaching Shouchun illness struck on the road—Jun ordered Zan lead baggage train back first.
translations.idiomatic: Sick short of Shouchun—he convoyed supplies homeward.

sentences.zh: 魏將蔣班以步騎四千追贊。

translations.literal: Wei general Jiang Ban with four thousand foot and horse pursued Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ban chased with four thousand.

sentences.zh: 贊病困，不能整陳，知必敗，乃解曲蓋印綬付弟子以歸，曰：「吾自為將，破敵搴旗，未嘗負敗。

translations.literal: Zan, sick and trapped, could not form ranks—knowing sure defeat he unfastened canopy seals and ribbons handing them to disciples to carry home, saying, “I have been general—breaking foes seizing banners—never tasted defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Too ill to fight—he sent seals home—‘I never fled until today.’

sentences.zh: 今病困兵羸，眾寡不敵，汝速去矣，俱死無益於國，適所以快敵耳。

translations.literal: Now illness wastes troops—numbers unmatched—you flee fast—dying together aids state nothing—only pleases foe.”
translations.idiomatic: Joint death gifts Wei—run.”

sentences.zh: 」弟子不肯受，拔刀欲斫之，乃去。

translations.literal: Disciples refused—he drew blade as if to strike—then they left.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened disciples until they ran.

sentences.zh: 初，讚為將，臨敵必先被發叫天，因抗音而歌，左右應之，畢乃進戰，戰無不克。

translations.literal: Earlier when Zan was general facing foe he always loosed hair, cried to Heaven, then sang loud voice while companions answered—only then advanced—battle never failed.
translations.idiomatic: His battle ritual: hair down, hymn to sky, then charge—undefeated.

sentences.zh: 及敗，歎曰：「吾戰有常術，今病困若此，固命也！

translations.literal: At defeat he sighed, “My warfare had fixed method—now sickness wastes me—solid fate!”
translations.idiomatic: “This is heaven—not tactics,” he said at the end.

sentences.zh: 」遂被害，時年七十三，眾庶痛惜焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed—seventy-three sui—common folk mourned.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three—Wu wept.

sentences.zh: 二子略、平，並為大將。〉

translations.literal: Two sons Lüe and Ping—both became grand generals.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Lüe and Ping rose to high command.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蜀使來聘，將軍孫儀、孫邵綝恂等欲因會殺峻。

translations.literal: That year Shu envoy came courting—generals Sun Yi, Sun Shao, Sun Lin’s kin Xun and others wished to use the banquet to kill Jun.
translations.idiomatic: During Shu’s embassy Sun Yi, Sun Shao, Sun Xun and allies plotted Jun’s murder at the feast.

sentences.zh: 事洩，儀等自殺，死者數十入，並及公主魯育。

translations.literal: Plot leaked—Yi and others committed suicide—several tens died (the transmitted tally may be corrupt)—including Princess Lu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They were exposed—dozens suicided—Princess Lu Yu among them.

sentences.zh: 峻欲城廣陵，朝臣知其不可城，而畏之莫敢言。

translations.literal: Jun wished to wall Guangling—court knew it impossible yet feared him—none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Jun dreamed of fortifying Guangling—ministers stayed mute in fear.

sentences.zh: 唯滕胤諫止，不從，而功竟不就。

translations.literal: Only Teng Yin remonstrated—Jun ignored—works never finished.
translations.idiomatic: Yin alone protested—the mad wall died unfinished.

sentences.zh: 其明年，文欽說峻徵魏，峻使欽與呂據、車騎劉纂、鎮南朱異、前將軍唐諮自江都人淮、泗，以圖青、徐。

translations.literal: Next year Wen Qin urged Jun to campaign Wei—Jun dispatched Qin with Lü Ju, chariot-general Liu Zuan, south-pacifier Zhu Yi, forward-general Tang Zi from Jiangdu into Huai and Si aiming at Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Year after, Qin talked Jun into another thrust—hosts left Jiangdu for Qing-Xu.

sentences.zh: 峻與胤至石頭，因餞之，領從者百許人入據營。

translations.literal: Jun and Yin reached Stone Citadel—seeing them off he led some hundred followers into Ju’s camp.
translations.idiomatic: At Stone Citadel Jun played farewell—then pushed into Lü Ju’s lines with a hundred guard.

sentences.zh: 據禦軍齊整，峻惡之，稱心痛去。

translations.literal: Ju’s troops stood crisp—Jun hated it—claimed heart pain and left.
translations.idiomatic: Ju’s crisp drill spooked Jun—he fled feigning chest pain.

sentences.zh: 遂夢為諸葛恪所擊，恐懼發病死，時年三十八，以後事付綝。

translations.literal: Then he dreamed Zhuge Ke struck him—terror broke him—sick unto death—thirty-eight sui—entrusted aftermath to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Nightmares of Ke—Jun died at thirty-eight—passed power to Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 孫綝字子通，與峻同祖。

translations.literal: Sun Lin, courtesy name Zitong, shared ancestors with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin (Zitong)—Jun’s cousin.

sentences.zh: 綝父綽為安民都尉。

translations.literal: Lin’s father Chuo was Commandant Who Pacifies the People.
translations.idiomatic: Father Sun Chuo held pacification command.

sentences.zh: 綝始為偏將軍，及峻死，為待中武衛將軍，領中外諸軍事，代知朝政。

translations.literal: Lin began as Major-General—when Jun died he became Palace Attendant, General Who Guards the Martial, commanding inner and outer armies, replacing him in managing court.
translations.idiomatic: Major to regent—Jun’s death made Lin armed chamberlain of all hosts.

sentences.zh: 呂據聞之大恐，與諸督將連名，共表薦滕胤為丞相，綝以胤為大司馬，代呂岱駐武昌。

translations.literal: Lü Ju heard and panicked—jointly with commanders memorialized recommending Teng Yin as Chancellor—Lin made Yin Grand Marshal replacing Lü Dai at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ju petitioned Yin as chancellor—Lin banished Yin to Grand Marshal at Wuchang instead.

sentences.zh: 據引兵還，使人報胤，欲共廢綝。

translations.literal: Ju led troops back and sent word to Yin—they meant jointly to depose Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ju reversed course and urged Teng Yin to sack Sun Lin together.

sentences.zh: 綝聞之，遣從兄慮將兵逆據於江都，使中使敕文欽、劉纂、唐諮等合眾擊據，遣侍中左將軍華融、中書丞丁晏告胤取據，並喻胤宜速去意，胤自以禍及，因留融、晏，勒兵自衛，召典軍揚崇、將軍孫諮，告以綝為亂，迫融等使有書難綝。

translations.literal: Hearing this Lin dispatched his cousin Sun Lü with troops to intercept Ju at Jiangdu; sent inner envoys ordering Wen Qin, Liu Zuan, Tang Zi and others to unite hosts and strike Ju; dispatched Palace Attendant General of the Left Hua Rong and Secretariat Deputy Ding Yan to notify Yin to seize Ju while instructing Yin he must flee swiftly—Yin judged calamity had reached him—thereupon detained Rong and Yan, mobilized troops for self-defense, summoned Army Clerk Yang Chong and general Sun Zi, declared Lin rebel, forced Rong and others to draft letters challenging Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin bottled Ju at Jiangdu while envoys pressured Yin; Yin held Hua Rong hostage, armed his household, and denounced Lin.

sentences.zh: 綝不聽，表言胤反，許將軍劉丞以封爵，使率兵騎急攻圍胤。

translations.literal: Lin refused listening—memorialized that Yin rebelled—promised general Liu Cheng enfeoffment—had him lead horse troops to storm and besiege Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin branded Yin traitor and threw Liu Cheng’s riders at his compound.

sentences.zh: 胤又劫融等使詐詔發兵。

translations.literal: Yin again coerced Rong and others to forge edict raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to fake an outbreak order through Hua Rong.

sentences.zh: 融等不從，胤皆殺之。

translations.literal: Rong and others refused—Yin slew them all.
translations.idiomatic: When they balked he cut them down.

sentences.zh: 〈文士傳曰：華融字德蕤，廣陵江都人。

translations.literal: The Wen shi zhuan states: Hua Rong, courtesy name Derui, was a man of Jiangdu in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Literary tradition: Hua Rong (Derui) of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 祖父避亂，居山陰蕊山下。

translations.literal: His grandfather fled turmoil and dwelt beneath Ruirui Mountain in Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors fled war to Shanyin hills.

sentences.zh: 時皇象亦寓居山陰，吳郡張溫來就像學，欲得所舍。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Xiang also lodged in Shanyin—Zhang Wen of Wu commandery came to Xiang for study and sought lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Calligrapher Huang Xiang shared the hamlet—Zhang Wen studied there.

sentences.zh: 或告溫曰：「蕊山下有華德蕤者，雖年少，美有令志，可舍也。

translations.literal: Someone told Wen: “Below Ruirui Mountain dwells Hua Derui—young yet fine in aspiration—lodging may be had there.”
translations.idiomatic: Locals sent Zhang Wen to Hua Rong’s gate.

sentences.zh: 」溫遂止融家，朝夕談講。

translations.literal: Wen therefore lodged at Rong’s house—morning and evening they conversed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen roomed with Hua Rong and talked night and day.

sentences.zh: 俄而溫為選部尚書，乃擢融為太子庶子，遂知名顯達。

translations.literal: Soon Wen became Director of Selection—thereupon promoted Rong to Palace Attendant to the Heir—thus he rose famed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wen ran appointments he lifted Hua Rong to tutor staff—fame followed.

sentences.zh: 融子諝，黃門郎，與融並見害。

translations.literal: Rong’s son Xu was Gentleman at the Yellow Gates—perished with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Son Hua Xu died beside him.

sentences.zh: 次子譚，以才辯稱，晉秘書監。〉

translations.literal: Second son Tan famed for eloquence—became Jin Palace Library Director.
translations.idiomatic: Younger son Tan won Jin office as library chief.

sentences.zh: 胤顏色不變，談笑若常。

translations.literal: Yin’s color never changed—talked and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin faced death smiling.

sentences.zh: 或勸胤引兵至蒼龍門，「將士見公出，必皆委綝就公」。

translations.literal: Some urged Yin to lead troops to Azure Dragon Gate—“when soldiers see Your Excellency emerge they will surely abandon Lin for you.”
translations.idiomatic: Counsel said: march on Azure Dragon Gate—the guard would flip.

sentences.zh: 時夜已半，胤恃與據期。

translations.literal: Night was already half spent—Yin relied on his rendezvous with Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Midnight—Yin still waited for Lü Ju.

sentences.zh: 又難舉兵向富，乃約令部曲，說呂侯以在近道，故皆為胤盡死，無離散者。

translations.literal: Again finding it hard to raise arms toward the palaces (the transmitted graph here is corrupt)—thereupon instructed retainers—explaining Marquis Lü was on nearby roads—therefore all fought to death for Yin without scattering.
translations.idiomatic: He told his men Ju was close—hold the line—but Ju never came.

sentences.zh: 時大風，比曉，據不至。

translations.literal: Great wind blew—by dawn Ju had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Gale till dawn—no Ju.

sentences.zh: 綝兵大會，遂殺及將士數十人，夷胤三族。

translations.literal: Lin’s troops massacred—thereupon slew Yin and several tens of officers—extinguished Yin’s three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin stormed in—slaughtered Yin’s clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以為孫綝雖凶虐，與滕胤宿無嫌隙，胤若且順綝意，出鎮武昌，豈徒免當時之禍，仍將永保元吉，而犯機觸害，自取夷滅，悲夫！〉

translations.literal: Your servant Pei Songzhi judges that though Sun Lin was cruel and violent he bore Yin no old grudge—had Yin temporized with Lin’s will and gone out to garrison Wuchang—not only would he have escaped immediate calamity—he might long have kept supreme good fortune—yet he brushed hazard and courted ruin—self-inviting extinction—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi: Yin could have taken Wuchang and lived—instead he chose martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 綝遷大將軍，假節，封永寧侯，負貴倨傲，多行無禮。

translations.literal: Lin advanced to Grand General—credential insignia—enfeoffed marquis of Yongning—bearing rank proud and rude—acting ceaselessly without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin grabbed Yongning marquisate and swaggered.

sentences.zh: 初，峻從弟慮與諸葛恪之謀，峻厚之，至右將軍、無難督，授節蓋，平九官事。

translations.literal: Earlier Jun’s cousin Lü had joined Zhuge Ke’s plot—Jun favored him—to General of the Right, Chief of “No Difficulty,” granting insignia and canopy, adjudicating nine palaces’ affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü had backed Ke—Jun raised him to right general and inner-court fixer.

sentences.zh: 綝遇慮薄於峻時，慮怒，與將軍王惇謀殺綝。

translations.literal: Lin treated Lü more coldly than Jun had—Lü grew angry—conspired with general Wang Dun to murder Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin snubbed Sun Lü—Lü plotted with Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 綝殺惇。

translations.literal: Lin slew Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Lin executed Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 慮服藥死。

translations.literal: Lü took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü swallowed poison.

sentences.zh: 魏大將軍諸葛誕舉壽春叛，保城請降。

translations.literal: Wei Grand General Zhuge Dan raised Shouchun in revolt—held the city suing for surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan rebelled in Wei and offered Wu the city.

sentences.zh: 吳遣文欽、唐諮、全端、全懌等三萬人救之。

translations.literal: Wu dispatched Wen Qin, Tang Zi, Quan Duan, Quan Yi and others—thirty thousand men—to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent thirty thousand under Wen Qin and Quan brothers.

sentences.zh: 魏鎮南將軍王基圍入誕。

translations.literal: Wei south-pacifying general Wang Ji invested wall against Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji tightened the Wei ring around Dan.

sentences.zh: 欽等突圍城。

translations.literal: Qin and others burst the siege lines.
translations.idiomatic: Relief column punched out.

sentences.zh: 魏悉中外軍二十餘萬增誕之圍。

translations.literal: Wei mobilized inner and outer armies over two hundred thousand to thicken Dan’s investment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stacked two hundred thousand more on the siege.

sentences.zh: 朱異帥三萬人屯安豐城，為文欽勢。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi commanded thirty thousand garrisoned Ancheng—supporting Wen Qin’s posture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi camped at Ancheng to back Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏兗州刺史州泰據異於陽淵，異敗退，為泰所追，死傷二干人。

translations.literal: Wei Yanzhou Inspector Zhou Tai checked Yi at Yangyuan—Yi defeated withdrew—Tai pursued—dead and wounded two thousand (the transmitted numeral may be corrupt).
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tai routed Zhu Yi—two thousand casualties.

sentences.zh: 林於是大發率出屯鑊裡，復遣異率將軍丁奉、黎斐等五萬人攻魏，留輜重於都陸。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon raised hosts in force encamping at Huoli—again sent Yi leading generals Ding Feng, Li Fei and others fifty thousand attacking Wei—left baggage at Dulü.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin stacked fifty thousand under Zhu Yi at Huoli—supplies at Dulü.

sentences.zh: 異屯黎漿，遣將軍任度、張震等慕勇敢六千人，於屯西六里為浮橋夜渡，築偃月壘。

translations.literal: Yi camped at Lijiang—sent generals Ren Du, Zhang Zhen and others recruiting six thousand brave—six li west of camp built pontoon bridge by night—raised crescent rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi tried night bridges and moon bastions west of camp.

sentences.zh: 為魏監軍石苞及州泰所破，軍卻退就高。

translations.literal: Wei Army Supervisor Shi Bao and Zhou Tai smashed them—army fell back to heights.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao and Zhou Tai crushed the bridgehead.

sentences.zh: 異復作車箱圍趣五木城。

translations.literal: Yi again fashioned cart-box siege aiming at Wumu fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi shifted to wagon-wall tactics toward Wumu.

sentences.zh: 苞、泰攻異，異敗歸，而魏太山太守胡烈以奇兵五千詭道襲都陸，盡焚異資糧。

translations.literal: Bao and Tai attacked Yi—Yi fled back—Wei Taishan governor Hu Lie with five thousand surprise troops by hidden track struck Dulü—burned Yi’s provisions entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie torched Zhu Yi’s depot at Dulü.

sentences.zh: 綝授兵三萬人使異死戰，異不從，綝斬之於鑊裡，而遣弟恩救。

translations.literal: Lin handed thirty thousand troops ordering Yi fight to death—Yi refused—Lin beheaded him at Huoli—sent younger brother En to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin executed Zhu Yi for disobedience—sent Sun En forward.

sentences.zh: 會誕敗引還。

translations.literal: When Dan fell they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dan’s fall ended the relief war.

sentences.zh: 綝既不能拔出誕，而喪敗士眾，自戮名將，莫不怨之。

translations.literal: Lin failed to extricate Dan yet wasted armies—personally executed a famed general—none failed to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu blamed Lin for killing Zhu Yi and losing Dan.

sentences.zh: 綝以孫亮始親政事，多所難問，甚懼。

translations.literal: Lin because Sun Liang began personally handling government affairs—asking many challenging questions—grew greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Boy emperor Liang asked hard questions—Lin panicked.

sentences.zh: 還建業，稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Returned Jianye—claimed illness and skipped court.
translations.idiomatic: He hid in private claiming sickness.

sentences.zh: 築室幹朱雀橋南，使弟威遠將軍據入蒼龍宿衛，弟武衛將軍恩、偏將軍幹、長水校尉闓分屯諸營，欲以專朝自固。

translations.literal: Built mansion south of Vermilion Sparrow Bridge—sent younger brother distant-guard general Ju into Azure Dragon palace guard—younger brother Guard Martial general En, Major-General Gan, Colonel of Long Rivers Kai—each garrisoned camps—intending to monopolize court and secure self.
translations.idiomatic: Ringed the capital with brothers in every gate camp.

sentences.zh: 亮內嫌綝，乃推魯育見殺本末，責怒虎林督朱熊、熊弟外部督朱損不匡正孫峻，乃令丁奉殺熊於虎林，殺損於建業。

translations.literal: Liang inwardly loathed Lin—thereupon pressed how Princess Lu Yu met death from root to tip—blazing at Forest Tiger colonel Zhu Xiong and younger brother outer colonel Zhu Sun for failing to correct Sun Jun—ordered Ding Feng slay Xiong at Forest Tiger—Sun at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Liang avenged Princess Lu Yu—executed Zhu Xiong brothers for Jun’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 綝入諫不從，亮遂與公主魯班、太常全尚、將軍劉承議誅綝。

translations.literal: Lin entered remonstrating—Liang did not heed—Liang then with Princess Lu Ban, Chamberlain Quan Shang, general Liu Cheng plotted executing Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang allied with Ban, Quan Shang, Liu Cheng to kill Lin.

sentences.zh: 亮妃，綝從姊女也，以其謀告綝。

translations.literal: Liang’s consort was Lin’s cousin’s daughter—she reported the plot to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: The empress—Lin’s cousin—whispered to Lin.

sentences.zh: 綝率眾夜襲全尚，遣弟恩殺劉承於蒼龍門外，遂圍宮。

translations.literal: Lin led hosts night-assaulting Quan Shang—sent younger brother En slaying Liu Cheng outside Azure Dragon Gate—thereupon besieged palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lin struck Quan Shang—murdered Liu Cheng—surrounded the palace.

sentences.zh: 〈江表傳曰：亮召全尚息黃門侍郎紀密謀，曰：「孫綝專勢，輕小於孤。

translations.literal: The Jiang Biao Zhuan states: Liang summoned Quan Shang’s son Gentleman at Yellow Gates Ji for secret counsel—“Sun Lin monopolizes power—belittles me—the orphan.”
translations.idiomatic: Liang told Quan Ji how Lin slighted the throne.

sentences.zh: 孤見敕之，使速上岸，為唐諮等作援，而留湖中，不上岸一步。

translations.literal: “I ordered him ashore fast to aid Tang Zi—yet he lingers mid-lake—not one step on bank.”
translations.idiomatic: He accused Lin of loafing on the lake.

sentences.zh: 又委罪硃異，擅殺功臣，不先表聞。

translations.literal: “Further shifted blame to Zhu Yi—executed worthy minister without prior memorial.”
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zhu Yi’s murder.

sentences.zh: 築第橋南，不復朝見。

translations.literal: “Built mansion bridge south—no longer attends audience.”
translations.idiomatic: Lin skipped court from his riverside villa.

sentences.zh: 此為自在，無復所畏，不可久忍。

translations.literal: “Such unconstrained arrogance—I cannot long endure.”
translations.idiomatic: Pride unbearable.

sentences.zh: 今規取之，卿父作中軍都督，使密嚴整士馬，孤當自出臨橋，帥宿衛虎騎、左右無難一時圍之。

translations.literal: “Now I plot seizure—you father commands central army—secretly ready horse and arms—I shall personally reach bridge leading palace tiger-cavalry, left-right No Difficulty corps surrounding him at once.”
translations.idiomatic: Plan: Quan Shang mobilizes—Liang leads guards at bridge.

sentences.zh: 作版詔敕綝所領皆解散，不得舉手，正爾自得之。

translations.literal: “Issue tablet edict dissolving Lin’s commands—no resistance—thus seize him.”
translations.idiomatic: Forged order disbands Lin’s troops.

sentences.zh: 卿去，但當使密耳。

translations.literal: “You depart—only absolute secrecy.”
translations.idiomatic: Tell no one.

sentences.zh: 卿宣詔語卿父，勿令卿母知之，女人既不曉大事，且綝同堂姊，邂逅洩漏，誤孤非小也。

translations.literal: “Announce edict to your father—do not let your mother know—women grasp not great affairs—and Lin is cousin by hall—chance leak ruins me beyond measure.”
translations.idiomatic: Warned Quan Ji to hide from mother—she was Lin’s kin.

sentences.zh: 」紀承詔，以告尚，尚無遠慮，以語紀母。

translations.literal: Ji received edict—reported to Shang—Shang lacked far sight—told Ji’s mother.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shang told his wife anyway.

sentences.zh: 母使人密語綝。

translations.literal: Mother sent secret word to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: She tipped Sun Lin.

sentences.zh: 綝夜發嚴兵廢亮，比明，兵已圍宮。

translations.literal: Lin night-mobilized crack troops deposing Liang—by dawn troops ringed palace.
translations.idiomatic: Lin struck first—palace under arms by dawn.

sentences.zh: 亮大怒，上馬，帶鞬執弓欲出，曰：「孤大皇帝之適子，在位已五年，誰敢不從者？

translations.literal: Liang raged—mounted horse—belt quiver grasped bow intending exit—“I am Great Emperor’s heir son—five years on throne—who dares disobey?”
translations.idiomatic: Boy emperor reached for bow—claimed mandate.

sentences.zh: 」侍中近臣及乳母共牽攀止之，乃不得出，嘆吒二日不食，罵其妻曰：「爾父憒憒，敗我大事！

translations.literal: Palace attendants and wet nurses together dragged him—could not exit—sighed two days without eating—reviled his wife—“Your father muddle-headed—ruined my great affair!”
translations.idiomatic: Women restrained him—he starved and cursed Quan clan.

sentences.zh: 」又呼紀，紀曰：「臣父奉詔不謹，負上，無面目復見。

translations.literal: Again summoned Ji—Ji said—“My father failed edict—betrayed sovereign—no face to see again.”
translations.idiomatic: Quan Ji chose suicide over shame.

sentences.zh: 」因自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He killed himself.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：亮傳稱亮少聰慧，勢當先與紀謀，不先令妻知也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Liang’s biography calls Liang clever youth—plot ought first consult Ji—not first let wife know.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng doubts chronology—smart boy would not tell wife first.

sentences.zh: 江表傳說漏洩有由，於事為詳矣。〉

translations.literal: Jiang Biao zhuan’s leak explanation follows cause—matters stand detailed therein.
translations.idiomatic: Pei accepts Jiang Biao leak narrative as fuller.

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳盂宗告廟廢亮，召群司儀曰：「少帝荒病昏亂，不可以處大位，承宗廟，以告先帝廢之。

translations.literal: Ordered Superintendent of the Household Meng Zong announce temples deposing Liang—summoned gathered officers—“Young emperor wasteland-sick muddled mad—may not occupy great seat—carry ancestral temples—therefore announcing prior emperor’s temples—deposing him.”
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zong read Lin’s deposition of Liang before altars.

sentences.zh: 諸君若有不同者，下異議。

translations.literal: “If gentlemen harbor dissent—voice contrary below.”
translations.idiomatic: Lin dared opposition to speak.

sentences.zh: 」皆震怖。

translations.literal: All trembled terror.
translations.idiomatic: Silence of fear.

sentences.zh: 曰：「唯將軍令。

translations.literal: They said—“Only the general’s command.”
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers bent knee.

sentences.zh: 」綝遣中書郎李祟奪亮璽綬，以亮罪狀班告遠近。

translations.literal: Lin dispatched Secretariat Gentleman Li Chong seizing Liang’s seals and ribbons—broadcast Liang’s crimes near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Lin seized seals and blackened Liang’s name.

sentences.zh: 尚書桓彝不肯署名，綝怒殺之。

translations.literal: Director Huan Yi refused signing—Lin slew him in wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi died refusing the coup paper.

sentences.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：彝，魏尚書令階之弟。

translations.literal: Han Jin Chunqiu states: Yi—younger brother of Wei Director Huan Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi was brother of Wei minister Huan Jie.

sentences.zh: 《吳錄》曰：晉武帝問薛瑩吳之名臣，瑩對稱彝有忠貞之節。〉

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Jin Wudi asked Xue Ying Wu’s famed ministers—Ying praised Yi’s loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Jin emperor later cited Huan Yi as Wu martyr.

sentences.zh: 典軍施正勸綝徵立琅邪王休，綝從之。

translations.literal: Army Clerk Shi Zheng urged Lin summon and enthrone Prince Langye Xiu—Lin followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zheng talked Lin into king Huima—Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 遣宗正楷奉書於休曰：

translations.literal: Dispatched Director of Imperial Clan Kai bearing letter to Xiu saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kai carried summons to Xiu:

sentences.zh: 綝以薄才，見授大任，不能輔導陛下。

translations.literal: Lin by slender talent received great charge—unable to tutor guidance Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The indictment opens with Lin’s sham confession that he failed as regent.

sentences.zh: 頃月以來，多所造立。

translations.literal: These recent months—many creations established.
translations.idiomatic: It lists Liang’s alleged novelty-building excesses.

sentences.zh: 親近劉承，悅於美色；

translations.literal: Favored Liu Cheng—delighted in beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Charges dalliance with Liu Cheng and palace women.

sentences.zh: 發吏民婦女，料其好者，留於宮內，取兵弟十八已下三千餘人，習之苑中，連日續夜，大小呼嗟，敗壞藏中矛戈五千餘枚，以作戲具。

translations.literal: Drafted civilian women—grading fairest—detained inside palace—recruited soldier youths eighteen and below over three thousand—drilled them in park—days linked nights—great and small wailed—ruined armory spears and halberds over five thousand—fashioned play gear.
translations.idiomatic: Monstrous catalog of Liang’s alleged orgies and toy navy.

sentences.zh: 朱據先帝舊臣，子男熊、損皆承父之基，以忠議自立，昔殺小主。

translations.literal: Zhu Ju prior emperor old minister—sons Xiong and Sun both inherited father base—stood by loyal counsel—yet killed junior lord.
translations.idiomatic: Claims Zhu heirs murdered princess—distorts truth.

sentences.zh: 自是大主所創，帝不復精其本未，便殺熊、損，諫不見用。

translations.literal: Since then Great Princess authored affair—emperor never examined root tip—then slew Xiong and Sun—remonstrance unused.
translations.idiomatic: Blames Liang for Zhu executions without hearing Lin’s guilt.

sentences.zh: 諸下莫不側息。

translations.literal: Underlings none failed to hold breath.
translations.idiomatic: Court terrified into silence.

sentences.zh: 帝於宮中作小船三百餘艘，成以金銀，師工晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Emperor inside palace built small boats over three hundred—gold and silver clad—artisans day night ceaseless.
translations.idiomatic: Accuses toy fleet waste.

sentences.zh: 太常全尚，累世受恩，不能督諸宗親，而全端等委城就魏。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Quan Shang—generations receiving grace—unable to supervise clan kin—while Quan Duan and others surrendered cities to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Smears Quan clan treason.

sentences.zh: 尚位過重，曾無一言以諫陛下，而與敵往來，使傳國消息，懼必傾危社稷。

translations.literal: Shang rank overly weighty—never one word remonstrating Majesty—yet trafficked with foe—transmitting state messages—I fear certain overturn of altars.
translations.idiomatic: Claims Quan Shang spied for Wei.

sentences.zh: 推案舊典，運集大王，輒以今月二十七日擒尚斬承。

translations.literal: Pushing investigation old precedent—fortune gathers Great King—therefore twenty-seventh of this month seized Shang executed Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Announces staged arrests— date fixed.

sentences.zh: 以帝為會稽王，遣楷牽迎。

translations.literal: Demoting emperor Prince of Kuaiji—dispatching Kai escorting welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Deposes Liang to Kuaiji prince—sends escort for Xiu.

sentences.zh: 百寮喁喁。

translations.literal: Hundred officials murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucracy voiced obedience.

sentences.zh: 立任道側。

translations.literal: Stood waiting along roadway.
translations.idiomatic: They lined the route for new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 綝奉牛酒詣休，休不受，齎詣左將軍張布。

translations.literal: Lin carried cattle wine visiting Xiu—Xiu refused—had them forwarded to General of the Left Zhang Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin’s peace gifts went to Zhang Bu—Xiu declined face-to-face.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，出怨言曰：「徹廢少主時，多勸吾自為之者。

translations.literal: Wine heated—bitter words emerged—“When we utterly deposed young sovereign—many urged me take throne myself.”
translations.idiomatic: Drunk Lin boasted he could have been emperor.

sentences.zh: 吾以陛下賢明，故迎之。

translations.literal: “I deemed Your Majesty sagely enlightened—therefore welcomed you.”
translations.idiomatic: Claims he chose Xiu for virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝非我不立，今上禮見拒，是與凡臣無異，當復改圖耳。

translations.literal: “Emperor without me would not stand—now courtesy visit refused—no different from common minister—must scheme anew.”
translations.idiomatic: Threatens another coup if snubbed.

sentences.zh: 」布以言聞休，休銜之。

translations.literal: Bu reported speech to Xiu—Xiu nursed grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bu warned Xiu—resentment seeded.

sentences.zh: 鞏其有變，數加賞賜，又復加恩侍中，與綝分省文書。

translations.literal: Fearing he might stir change—the received character here is probably a scribal error for fear—repeatedly piled rewards—again extended grace as Palace Attendant—sharing Lin province over documents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu feared Lin would bolt—showered honors and busywork to watch him.

sentences.zh: 或有告綝懷怨侮上欲圖反者，休執以付綝，綝殺之。

translations.literal: Someone reported Lin nursed grievance insulting superior plotting revolt—Xiu seized accuser handing to Lin—Lin slew him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu fed Lin a false informer—Lin killed him—proving brutality.

sentences.zh: 由是愈懼，因孟宗求出屯武昌，休許焉，盡敕所督中營精兵萬餘人，皆令裝載，所取武庫兵器，咸令給與。

translations.literal: Thereby Lin grew more fearful—through Meng Zong begged posting garrison Wuchang—Xiu permitted—full order to crack troops over ten thousand he commanded—all directed loaded—armory weapons requested—all granted.
translations.idiomatic: Lin fled toward Wuchang with elite ten thousand—throne armed him freely.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳曆》曰：綝求中書兩郎，典知荊州諸軍事，主者奏中書不應外出，休特聽之，其所請求，一皆給與。〉

translations.literal: Wu li states: Lin begged two Secretariat gentlemen managing Jingzhou military affairs—chief memorialized Secretariat ought not post outward—Xiu specially permitted—all requests granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wu li: Xiu let Lin pick secretaries for Jingzhou staff.

sentences.zh: 將軍魏邈說休曰「綝居外必有變」，武衛士施朔又告「綝欲反有徵」休密問張布，布與丁奉謀於會殺綝。

translations.literal: General Wei Mi advised Xiu—“Lin abroad certain brings mutiny”—Palace guardsman Shi Shuo again reported—“Lin plots revolt with signs”—Xiu secretly questioned Zhang Bu—Bu with Ding Feng plotted banquet killing Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mi and Shi Shuo flagged coup—Xiu and Ding Feng laid feast trap.

sentences.zh: 綝死時年二十八。

translations.literal: Lin died aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin perished at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 休耽與峻、綝同族，特除其屬籍，稱之曰故峻、故綝雲​​。

translations.literal: Xiu—the opening character of the sentence is probably a scribal error for since—shared clan with Jun and Lin—therefore specially struck them from genealogy—calling them “late Jun” and “late Lin,” it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiu struck Sun Jun and Sun Lin from the imperial lineage—only “the late Jun” and “the late Lin” remained on the record.

sentences.zh: 休又下詔曰：「諸葛恪、滕胤、呂據蓋以無罪為峻、綝兄弟所見殘害，可為痛心，促皆改葬，各為祭奠。

translations.literal: Xiu further issued edict: “Zhuge Ke, Teng Yin, and Lü Ju were innocent yet slaughtered by Jun and Lin brothers—utterly heartbreaking—hasten reburial for each with sacrifices.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu ordered honorable reburial for Ke, Yin, and Ju—framed as innocent victims of the Sun cousins.

sentences.zh: 其罹恪等事見遠徙者，一切召還。」

translations.literal: “Those who suffered Ke affair and were banished afar—summon all back.”
translations.idiomatic: Exiles tied to Ke’s fall were recalled.

sentences.zh: 濮陽興

translations.literal: Puyang Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing

sentences.zh: 永安三年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。

translations.literal: Third year of Yongan the Commandant Yan Mi proposed Danyang lake-field works—building Puli Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan 3: Yan Mi pitched the Puli reclamation on Danyang’s lakes.

sentences.zh: 詔百官會議，咸以為用功多而田不保成，唯興以為可成。

translations.literal: Edict ordered hundred offices conference—all judged labor vast while fields might not hold—only Xing deemed it doable.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers called the dyke a boondoggle—Puyang Xing alone swore it would pay.

sentences.zh: 遂會諸兵民就作，功傭之費不可勝數，士卒死亡，或自賊殺，百姓大怨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon assembled troops and civilians to labor—merit-pay costs beyond counting—soldiers died—some killed each other—commoners bitterly resented.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée swelled—paymasters drowned—troops died in mutiny and accident—the delta cursed Xing’s name.

sentences.zh: 興遷為丞相，與休寵臣左將軍張共布相表裡，邦內失望。

translations.literal: Xing promoted Chancellor—joined Xiu’s favored minister General of the Left Zhang Bu (the transmitted text inserts a stray graph between the two syllables of the name)—mutual inside-out—the state inwardly despaired.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to chancellor, he teamed with Zhang Bu—Wu groaned at crony rule.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，休薨。

translations.literal: Seventh month seventh year Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu died in the seventh month of the seventh year of his era.

sentences.zh: 左典軍萬彧素與烏程侯孫皓善，乃勸興、布，於是興、布廢休適子而迎立皓。

translations.literal: Left Army Clerk Wan Yu long favored Marquis of Wucheng Sun Hao—thereupon urged Xing and Bu—thus Xing and Bu deposed Xiu’s heir son of proper line and welcomed Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yu talked Xing and Bu into skipping Xiu’s son for Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓既踐阼，加興侍中，領青州牧。

translations.literal: Once Hao mounted throne he added Xing Palace Attendant concurrent Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao bought loyalty with palace posts and a Qingzhou title.

sentences.zh: 俄彧譖興、布追悔前事。

translations.literal: Soon Yu slandered Xing and Bu—regretting prior deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yu then whispered that both ministers regretted enthroning him.

sentences.zh: 十一月朔入朝，皓因收興、布，徙廣州，道追殺之，夷三族。

translations.literal: First day eleventh month court entry—Hao thereupon seized Xing and Bu—banished Guangzhou—agents overtook them on road killing—extinguished three clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon Hao arrested them—marched them toward Guangzhou—had them killed en route—then wiped three degrees of kin.

translations.literal: Bracketed marginal rubric: Appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Section rubric: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：諸葛恪才氣幹略，邦人所稱，然驕且吝，周公無​​觀，況在於恪？

translations.literal: Appraisal says: Zhuge Ke’s talent, breath, capacity, and stratagem—the state praised them—yet arrogant and grudging (the Duke-of-Zhou phrase in the received text appears corrupt)—how much more Ke?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou: Wu admired Ke’s brilliance, but pride and deafness to counsel ruined him—a sage regent could scarcely have controlled such ego.

sentences.zh: 矜己陵人，能無敗乎！

translations.literal: Prizing self and trampling others—how avoid ruin!
translations.idiomatic: Vanity and contempt for peers doom any minister.

sentences.zh: 若躬行所與陸遜及弟融之書，則悔吝不至，何尤禍之有哉？

translations.literal: Had he personally lived the teachings of his letters to Lu Xun and to younger brother Rong—regret and blame would not have arrived—what ground for disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Had Ke practiced the humility he preached to Lu Xun and Zhuge Rong, he might have died in bed.

sentences.zh: 滕胤厲修士操，遵蹈規矩，而孫峻之時猶保其貴，必危之理也。

translations.literal: Teng Yin sternly cultivated gentleman conduct—trod rules and measures—yet under Sun Jun still preserved his nobility—this was inherently the logic of certain peril.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin’s rectitude could not save him once Jun turned butcher—virtue offered no armor.

sentences.zh: 峻、綝兇豎盈溢，固無足論者。

translations.literal: Jun and Lin—brutal boys overflowing wickedness—hardly worth extended discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun and Sun Lin were base plotters beneath serious debate.

sentences.zh: 濮陽興身居宰輔，慮不經國，協張布之邪，納萬彧之說，誅夷其宣矣。

translations.literal: Puyang Xing occupied chief counselor seat—thought did not traverse state—aided Zhang Bu’s crookedness—accepted Wan Yu’s counsel—extinction was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang Xing stood at the helm yet peddled Wan Yu’s intrigue and Zhang Bu’s faction—his annihilation was earned.
